findings: Remark 2.12 is the only bridge between Lemmas 2.9-2.11 (statements about arcs of the model E0) and curves of M; it is used at l.1093 and carries no proof. For the blunt spear, its truth needs the spear to be closed in M (an arc leaving through the shaft must not have its past end at a frontier point of psi(spear) outside psi(spear)).

Remark 2.12 is PROVED (WP-44e, 0 sorry) for the blunt spears of the surgery and inextensible causal curves of Reg M: the component is a spear arc (K-3 hypotheses of Lemma 2.10). The past end is on the head (the first point of a component has f = v, since just before it the curve is outside the closed spear, and read in the chart it is Le-below the entry point, with r below R) or at the axis (otherwise a bounded past end would be a limit in Reg M); the future end is on the shaft or at tau = +infinity. The remark's Lemma 2.9 half (curves of M through compact spears, crossing the axis) is not formalized: the surgery only uses Lemma 2.10's.

kb_proposals: FTC for a length: a Lipschitz f on [a,b] with k|f'| <= localDensity a.e. gives k|f(b)-f(a)| <= localLength (LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval + AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub; GX.E0Surgery.le_localLength_of_lipschitzOnWith). Combined with LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt_real it turns every pointwise density bound into a PulledLength edist bound.

A path Lipschitz in charts for a single developing map F has F o gamma.extend globally Lipschitz (Causal.Flat.isLocLip_pulled_iff); read coordinates back through continuous linear functionals of Minkowski 2 and ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith on a compact box (GX.E0Surgery.path_coords).

A clamped coordinate max(r, rho) is Lipschitz with derivative r' above rho and 0 elsewhere (IsLocalMin.deriv_eq_zero at r = rho): it gives 'leaving an annulus costs length' with no first-exit-time argument (GX.E0Surgery.clamp_le_edist).

In E0, Le x y gives x.1 <= y.1 (Le.norm_sub_le) and rad x <= rad y (Le.closed.2.1): along a causal arc both tau and r are monotone, which turns the end conditions of B21 Lemma 2.10 into order-theoretic ones.

A piecewise graph tau = min(c, f) (slice + spacelike graph) is acausal across the BTZ axis with no derivative criterion there: its height is max(tau - c, F_f), a max of two functions strictly increasing along the causal order (GX.E0Surgery.isSpacelikeDiscGraph_of_min; tau strictly increases along E0's Le between distinct points by Le.norm_sub_le, fst_lt_of_le_of_ne).

Write a piecewise radial function with max r (R/2) in place of r (GX.E0Surgery.discExt): it is globally continuous and equals each piece on its side, so continuity and compactness of its graph need no case analysis.
For HasDerivAt of (fun r => (f r)^2) use HasDerivAt.fun_pow (HasDerivAt.pow is for f^n as a Pi power and its instance path does not unify with Real's Semiring.toModule).

IsSpacelikeLipschitz is pointwise, hence local: if T = T' on an open O around x and T' is spacelike Lipschitz at x, so is T (GX.E0Surgery.IsSpacelikeLipschitzAt.congr, via IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn.restrict to V meet (e.target cap e.symm^-1 O)).

The topology field of Causal.Flat.IsCauchyComplete is free once the surface is spacelike Lipschitz: Causal.Flat.Cla.continuous_inducedLengthSpace_toSubtype (T2 M); and a compact spacelike Lipschitz set is complete (completeSpace_inducedLengthSpace_of_isCompact). Both live in Causal.Flat.Cla.CompactComplete, already in the closure of Causal.Flat.Classification.
LocalModel's (O2)/(O4') are proved (WP-43d): Spear's section variables hLine/hSC instantiate as E0LM.e0_globalBTZ and (fun {_} _ _ _ _ _ => E0LM.e0_secondCountable_of_cauchy).

An E0-morphism psi preserves the BTZ type: psi(paperInY x) in sing0 iff x is on the axis (Causal.CBG.mem_chartedSing_iff_of_liftPropOn e0_sing_mem + chartAt_self_eq; GX.E0Surgery.SpearSurgeryDatum.mem_S0_iff).

A Prop-valued regularity predicate of the form 'for every chart and every function g with (property of g relative to S), P(g)' must constrain g enough to be determined by S, or it is contradictory: here a spear graph function tau_S was free wherever the spear misses S (AUDIT-2 B1). Guard: prove a uniqueness lemma for g from the antecedents (GX.E0Surgery.eqOn_closedBall_of_rim_antecedent) and try to derive False from the predicate plus one datum before building on it.

A spear psi(spear v R) of an injective E0-chart is closed in a GH E0-manifold (GX.E0Surgery.isClosed_image_spearY): bounded-tau sequences have convergent subsequences in the chart; a climbing sequence puts the vertical line over its limit below the limit point (GloballyHyperbolic.isClosed_le), a monotone curve in a compact diamond, against E0Spear.spear_vertical_noLimit.

In a GH E0-manifold, J^-(S) minus S is I^-(S) for a Cauchy surface S (GX.E0Surgery.mem_Iminus_of_le_of_mem): p is in the closure of I^+(p) (E0LM.Jplus_subset_closure_Iplus with SingularFlatAxioms.mem_Zplus), J^+(S) is closed, and push-up. This gives Lemma 2.4's hypothesis p in I^-(S) for every BTZ point strictly below S on its line.

Two spears are disjoint as soon as each ray misses the other spear and one head misses the other spear (GX.E0Surgery.SpearSurgeryDatum.disjoint_of_head): follow the radial null segment from the ray to a common point, take the last entry into the closed second spear, and read the segment in the second chart through invFunOn (Causal.CBG.liftPropOn_invFunOn is an E0-morphism; IsEMorphismOn.map_le twice) - the entry is on the head. Heads shrink to the vertex, so thinning each spear against the finitely many others makes the family disjoint.

A causal curve of M inside the image of an injective E0-chart reads as a Le-increasing curve of E0 (GX.E0Surgery.SpearSurgeryDatum.le_of_causalCurve): Causal.IsEMorphismOn.causalCurveIn_invComp with invFunOn as left inverse, then E0Spear.ceY_le_iff, D.le_mono into range Sum.inr, E0Spear.D_le_rangeInr_iff, E0.le_top_iff.

To analyse the ends of an inextensible curve over a general interval I, reparametrise over R (Causal.Causality.Inextensible.reparam) and transport components (phi '' J_d = J by preconnectedness both ways); a bounded end in a compact part of a chart is then a limit at atBot/atTop, refuted by Inextensible.not_tendsto_atBot/atTop (Causal.Static). Reg M's hypotheses for these (closed J, strong causality, J(p) != {p}) come from M by causal convexity of Reg M (GX.E0Surgery.regM_facts, regM_Jminus_ne).

A spacelike graph is spacelike Lipschitz without any implicit function theorem: its height F (C^1, dF positive on the closed future cone at p0) is c-cone-increasing on a ball for c = (|dF o inr| + dF(1,0))/(2 dF(1,0)) < 1 (Riesz for |dF o inr| < dF(1,0), then the mean value theorem on segments), and Causal.Flat.Cla.exists_isSpacelikeLipschitzIn_zeroSet makes its zero set a Lipschitz graph (GX.E0Surgery.exists_ball_isConeIncreasingOn).

IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn admits a frame: prove cone-increase of F o g^-1 on g • W in whatever frame g is convenient (e.g. the frame of another surface's Lipschitz graph), then move back with IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn.smul isom_strongMorphism (GX.E0Surgery.isSpacelikeLipschitzAt_of_coneZeroSet').

Gluing two spacelike hypersurfaces along a cylinder ruled by null lines: use heights measured ALONG that null direction (the null-shift height of a Lipschitz graph, GX.E0Surgery.exists_nullShift, is cone-increasing and Lipschitz with no regularity), so they agree on the cylinder and the piecewise height is continuous and cone-increasing (cut segments at a crossing point).

In E0, d_tau develops to a constant null vector: btzPaperDev (tau - s, r, theta) = btzPaperDev (tau, r, theta) - s • nullToMink (2, 0, 0) (GX.E0Surgery.chartMap_shift), so tau-shifts are translations in every flat chart.

Completeness of an induced length by a Lipschitz exhaustion: if a function F on S is 1-Lipschitz for edist (prove it pathwise with le_localLength_of_lipschitzOnWith: Rademacher in ONE chart near each time, localDensity_chartSys_eq to read the density there, ae_of_local to globalise) and its sublevel sets are compact, Cauchy sequences converge (Causal.Flat.Cla.continuous_inducedLengthSpace_toSubtype_symm turns subspace convergence into length convergence). Clamp log r at R/2 so the function is locally constant near rims (GX.E0Surgery.SurgeryData.logRad).

A non-compact Cauchy surface by two closed sides: if F, P are closed in the spacetime, cover it, meet exactly along Sigma, F propagates forward and P backward along causal curves (local chart statements + IsClosed.Icc_subset_of_forall_mem_nhdsWithin), and every inextensible curve meets both, then Sigma is Cauchy once a causal curve inside Sigma is locally constant (GX.E0Surgery.SurgeryData.isCauchySurface_sigmaStar, §5g of GXScaffold.BTZ.Surgery). No compactness of Sigma and no intersection numbers are needed.

Reading a causal curve of M in an injective E0-chart near one of its points: GX.E0Surgery.SpearSurgeryDatum.eventually_le_coord gives, for s near t, e s = psi(u) with u in a prescribed open V and x <= u after t, u <= x before (le_of_causalCurve on the segment). With E0.calculus_le (r and f = tau - r/2 are nondecreasing along <=) a curve can leave a spear forward only through the shaft and backward only through the head.

A BTZ point q with s <= q for some s in a set S: s is BTZ and in the S0-component of q (SingularFlatAxioms.Jminus_subset_component); combine with IsFullFutureBTZRay.exists_eq_of_line to put q on a spear ray (GX.E0Surgery.exists_open_of_BTZ).

Pointwise spacelike (Lemma 2.7 off the axis) + height continuous on the closed cylinder already implies the integrated 'height strictly increasing along <= on {r <= R}, axis included' (GX.E0Surgery.isSpacelikeDiscGraph_of_isSpacelikeGraph): integrate along the straight segment of the development from the axis point, which has r = s r(y) > 0 for s > 0.
